## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `security` · `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `area:workflow` · `pm:queue`. Additive versioned scheme here; a cutover that refuses body-only signatures is the maintainer's

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-11T04:55Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Mandate:** condition 3 of ruling A on #22757 (`6105447950`) directs a hardening card if the scheme lacks replay protection, and the seat read that it does. The filing is ③.
- **Why p2 and `security`:** the hosted shape opens this door under ruling A. A captured signed request can be replayed, because the signed material carries no time. Kept at class level, as on the card.
- **Lane:** `packages/triggers/trigger-api` is `domain:services`. The sender-facing face (the documented recipe, and any `packages/spec` declaration of the header) is declared in the claim under the cross-domain exception path.
- **The contract question, answered:**
  - This card adds a **versioned** scheme beside the current one: a timestamp in the signed material, checked against a tolerance window. A request that claims the new scheme and fails it gets the same typed envelope a bad signature gets.
  - Body-only signatures keep working, ⛔ so no existing sender breaks in this card.
  - **Refusing body-only signatures** (the cutover) breaks every existing sender, so it goes to the maintainer as a decision. The claimant files it with the measured sender population: our own `http` node (#20628), the documented recipe, and HotCRM.
  - The flow `http` node's outbound signing (#20628) adopts the new scheme in the same PR if it is ours to change, and says so.
- **Order:** independent of #22757's segments (condition 3: ⛔ not folded). Either may land first.
- **Pins:**
  - a fresh timestamped request is accepted;
  - a replay outside the window is refused;
  - a stale timestamp with a valid body signature is refused;
  - CONTROL: a body-only signature still accepted, with a deprecation signal the claimant names.

A request that claims the new scheme and fails it gets the same typed envelope a bad signature gets. Body-only signatures keep working, so no existing sender breaks.
File surface, read on `origin/main` `e84aeb36c`:
- `packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts` (cross-domain, `domain:engine`'s package). Its header makes it "the ONE definition every ObjectStack sender signs with and every receiver verifies against", with "⛔ Never a second copy of this HMAC input anywhere". The versioned sign and verify go here, beside `signHttpBody`, plus its export line in `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`. Declared to the `domain:engine` seat 1 on #6367 before any edit, in this act.
- `packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts`: `verifySignature` (about `:94`–`:102`) computes its own copy of that HMAC input today. It verifies through the core definition instead and accepts the versioned scheme beside the body-only one, with a deprecation signal on the body-only arm.
- Tests beside both; `.changeset/22769-*.md` for `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/trigger-api`.
- ⛔ No change to what our senders send: `service-messaging`'s outbox and `service-automation`'s `http` node keep body-only `X-Objectstack-Signature`, because switching them breaks third-party receivers. ⛔ No `packages/spec`, no `packages/lint` text, no docs page; each is reported if the dev finds it owed. ⛔ No `plugin.ts` mount change (#22774's). Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- The cutover (refusing body-only) is the maintainer's. The dev measures the sender population (our two senders, the documented recipe, the lint explanation text; HotCRM is not readable from this container), and the seat files the decision card from that report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: "no path-derived mandate"; the default tier builds a clause-② card, and a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review follows before the queue)
Clause-②: yes
- It widens the inbound door's accept set (a new signature form) and adds a public export to `@objectstack/core`. The PR owes a contract-review-tier record before the queue.
Responsibility: `n/a — not a defect card`
Thread-read: 6105617130
Serial constraints cleared:
- No open PR touches `trigger-api/src/`, `core/src/security/http-signature.ts`, `service-messaging/src/http-sender.ts` or `http-nodes.ts` (11 open PRs' file lists, read at this stamp).
- PR #22779 (#22772, `domain:spec`) declares the trigger-api inbound-hook member in `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts`. It is disjoint from this surface. #22774 (the member's implementation, `pm:blocked`) will call the verifier this card changes, and whichever lands second adapts.

## Note from `domain:spec` seat 2: the inbound-hook contract now cites this card for the uniform-refusal question

`domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · `session_016njDy8ozy9B9Ns5Y8kAWEK` · 2026-10-11T07:47Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ no label change. This is information for the holder.

- **What the contract says.** PR #22779 (#22772, accepted `6106807013`, in the merge queue) declares `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook`. Its docblock now states the probe surface as it is:
  - an unknown flow and a wrong hook id answer one `404`;
  - but the hook is matched before the signature is verified;
  - so an unsigned anonymous post to a flow armed under the default hook id `default` answers `401` (or `503`, when the secret is unavailable) where an unarmed flow answers `404`. That reveals which flows exist.
- **What it leaves to this card.** The docblock ends that bullet: "Whether every unverified post should get one uniform refusal is the hardening card's question (#22769), not this contract's."
- **Read on `origin/main`:** `api-trigger.ts:225`–`:230` (the hook match) precedes the secret read (`:234`–`:246`) and `verifySignature` (`:247`), and `:159` defaults the hook id to `default`.
- It is the raw mount's shipped order, and within ruling A's "equal to self-hosted". So it is a hardening option for this card, not a defect of #22757's segments. The holder decides whether it rides this card's scheme change.
